back: A cost that stays the same in total when activity changes within the relevant range. Fixed cost per unit falls as output rises.
A cost that changes in total in proportion to activity. Variable cost per unit is constant.
A cost with a fixed element and a variable element, for example a bill with a standing charge plus a charge per unit.
A cost that is fixed within a range of activity and jumps to a higher amount when the range is exceeded.
(Cost at highest activity - cost at lowest activity) ÷ (highest activity - lowest activity).
Total cost at a level - (variable cost per unit × activity at that level). Check using the other level.
The range of activity over which the assumed cost behaviour is valid; estimates outside it are unreliable.

front: Why total cost per unit falls with output
back: Fixed costs are spread over more units while the variable cost per unit is constant.
It uses only two points and assumes a straight line, so unusual months and steps can distort it.
